**Issue #3058 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3058: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 41903860423](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41903860423) on `claude/link-google` (`c38b53a`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [rust (test tools, wasm)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41903860423/job/126834651467) | 7m 30s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom: most splits only need a longer matrix list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)`, or `rust (test <group>)`, whose crate groups split further, a crate's test binaries apart with `--lib`/`--test <name>`); for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`. Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`. Make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere (the e2e `WEIGHTS`, a slow test made faster or split across files), and when the split needs `ci.yml`'s matrix, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41907894741)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`rust (test tools, wasm)` took 7m30s. I measured it on this 4-core runner with no CI log access:

- The workspace compile takes 178 s (engine 144 s, cards 126 s at opt-level 2).
- The `jackioh` bin's unit tests take 181 s (391 tests). Three modules cause it:
  - `arena` takes 92 s. `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` is 79 s alone and `r747000_a_mid_skill_game_reproduces_and_replays` is 24 s.
  - `selfplay_records` takes 81 s. Its 2 tests play full-budget AI games.
  - `gate` takes 19 s.
- The other test binaries take about 22 s together.

The bot's part: make the two AI-game modules cheap by playing their whole games at a smaller node budget. The assertions stay as they are. That brings the bin tests from 181 s to 54 s, with all 391 passing. By my estimate the job still lands near 5m10, so the bot's part alone does not reach under 5 minutes with headroom.

**A person must edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** to finish the split. The exact lines are under Open questions. With them I estimate about 4m per group. These are estimates: setup and cache overhead is a guess of 50–70 s, and nothing here was timed on CI.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` | new `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) const TEST_BUDGET`; tests `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` and `r747000_a_mid_skill_game_reproduces_and_replays` play at it |
| `crates/tools/src/selfplay.rs` | `play_chunks` becomes a wrapper over new `play_chunks_at(…, budget, …)`; new `#[cfg(test)] play_at`; import `SearchBudget` |
| `crates/tools/src/selfplay_records.rs` | tests' `exported()` plays the 2 games once, at `TEST_BUDGET`, shared by both tests |

**Must not touch:**
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`
- `crates/engine`, `crates/ai`, `crates/cards`, `spec/`
- `crates/tools/tests/`
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (its header comment goes with the person's ci.yml edit)

There is no new ruling: no rules decision is made. The changed tests carry R850000, R747000 and R1676000, and the new comment cites R1489000 (a game with fallbacks is faulty). Test names are unchanged, so `spec check` is unaffected. CLAUDE.md rule 9 is met because the number is a named constant.

## Steps

1. **`crates/tools/src/arena.rs`**: insert this between the `ArenaGame` struct (ends near line 336) and `/// What a game came to…`:
   ```rust
   /// The budget a test decides at when it plays whole games to prove how a game is dealt, seated,
   /// replayed or filed, not how well it is played: `AI_GATE_BUDGET`'s search at about a quarter of its
   /// nodes and one determinization. At 60 nodes a seat falls back on two dozen decisions of a game,
   /// which R1489000 faults; 80 was the least that filed clean, and 150 leaves room.
   #[cfg(test)]
   pub(crate) const TEST_BUDGET: SearchBudget = SearchBudget {
       nodes: 150,
       lethal_nodes: 40,
       determinizations: 1,
       ..AI_GATE_BUDGET
   };
   ```
2. **`arena.rs`, test `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal`**: change `let games = setups(…)` to `let mut games = …`, then add this before `play_games`:
   ```rust
   for game in &mut games {
       game.self_budget = TEST_BUDGET;
   }
   ```
   Leave every assertion as it is.
3. **`arena.rs`, test `r747000_a_mid_skill_game_reproduces_and_replays`**: make the same change after its `setups(…)` call. Do not touch `two_self_agents_over_four_games_are_deterministic` (already daily) or the other arena tests.
4. **`crates/tools/src/selfplay.rs`**: change the import to `use jackioh_ai::{AI_GATE_BUDGET, SearchBudget, ai_generation, dev_game_config};`. Make `play_chunks` a wrapper and move its body into `play_chunks_at`. `run` stays untouched, which keeps rustfmt's layout of its call:
   ```rust
   pub(crate) fn play_chunks(base: &str, from: i32, games: i32, commit: &str,
       sink: impl FnMut(&[SelfplayGame]) -> anyhow::Result<()>) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
       play_chunks_at(base, from, games, commit, AI_GATE_BUDGET, sink)
   }
   /// `play_chunks` with both seats deciding at `budget`, which only a test lowers.
   fn play_chunks_at(base: &str, from: i32, games: i32, commit: &str, budget: SearchBudget,
       mut sink: impl FnMut(&[SelfplayGame]) -> anyhow::Result<()>) -> anyhow::Result<()> { /* the old body */ }
   ```
   Format the signatures as rustfmt does. In the body, replace `setups(base, start, count).par_iter()` with:
   ```rust
   let mut batch = setups(base, start, count);
   for game in &mut batch {
       game.self_budget = budget;
   }
   let played: Vec<(ArenaOutcome, f64)> = batch.par_iter()… // rest unchanged
   ```
   `setups` already sets `AI_GATE_BUDGET`, so production games are unchanged.
5. **`selfplay.rs`**: keep `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn play(base, from, games, commit)`, but its body becomes `play_at(base, from, games, commit, AI_GATE_BUDGET)`. Below it add:
   ```rust
   /// `play` with both seats deciding at `budget`, for a test that proves how a game files, not how
   /// well it is played.
   #[cfg(test)]
   pub(crate) fn play_at(base: &str, from: i32, games: i32, commit: &str, budget: SearchBudget)
       -> anyhow::Result<Vec<SelfplayGame>> { /* old body of play, calling play_chunks_at(base, from, games, commit, budget, |chunk| …) */ }
   ```
   The `selfplay::` tests keep calling `play(…)` and are unchanged.
6. **`crates/tools/src/selfplay_records.rs`, `mod tests`**: add `use crate::arena::TEST_BUDGET;` above `use crate::stats::…`, and replace `exported` with:
   ```rust
   /// The real exporter's lines for games `1..=games` of the base `records-test` on commit `abc123`,
   /// both played once for the two tests (game n does not depend on how many follow it).
   fn exported(games: usize) -> Vec<SelfplayGame> {
       static EXPORT: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<SelfplayGame>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
       let all = EXPORT
           .get_or_init(|| crate::selfplay::play_at("records-test", 1, 2, "abc123", TEST_BUDGET).unwrap());
       all[..games].to_vec()
   }
   ```
   The callers `exported(1)` and `exported(2)` stay as they are, since an integer literal infers `usize`.
7. Run `cargo fmt` on the three files, then the commands under Tests. If `selfplay_records` fails with "pN: n fallbacks", raise `TEST_BUDGET.nodes` (do not drop the fault assertion).

## Tests

No test is added, deleted or ignored. Three test groups change cost only. I ran the exact edits above in a scratch copy at `/tmp/exp`: fmt is clean, clippy `-D warnings` on `jackioh-tools` is clean, and these results held.

| Command | Expect |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- arena:: selfplay_records::` | 20 passed, 1 ignored, about 23 s (was 92 s + 81 s) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- selfplay::` | 7 passed, unchanged behaviour of `play`; slow (about 110 s) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::` | 391 passed, 5 ignored, about 55 s (was 181 s) |

The two tests that assert on the AI's play keep their assertions:
- `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` asserts identical hash and log with the agents swapped, a result, and the paired tally.
- The `selfplay_records` tests still assert that no game has faults or fallbacks.

A node budget has no clock in it, so determinism and replay hold at any budget.

Also run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh spec check`. The harness's checks need no extra step.

## Done when

- [ ] `TEST_BUDGET`, `play_chunks_at` and `play_at` exist as above; `run` and every production path are byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour.
- [ ] The three commands above pass, and the bin's non-fuzz, non-selfplay, non-positions tests finish in about a minute rather than three.
- [ ] fmt, clippy, `spec check`, the catalog check and the patches check pass; no `#[ignore]`, `allow` or assertion was added or removed.
- [ ] The PR body names the person's ci.yml part (Open questions) and states that the timings are local, not CI.
- [ ] Decision recorded: the budget was lowered (and one export shared) rather than moving the tests to daily, because the rules they prove are per-pull-request ones with no cheaper test holding them.
- [ ] Alternatives rejected: `stats.rs`'s `FEW` budget (60 nodes left `selfplay_records` with about 25 fallbacks per seat, and `FEW` the same); opt-level 2 for `jackioh-ai` (Cargo.toml's comment already measured it as a loss).

## Risks

- **A fallback threshold.** `selfplay_records` needs games with zero fallbacks. 60 nodes failed, 80 passed (9 s), 100 passed (18 s) and 150 passed (17 s). 150 is chosen for margin. A later AI or engine change could push a decision past the threshold. The fix is to raise `nodes`.
- **Shared export.** The `OnceLock` holds both tests' games. A panic inside `get_or_init` leaves it unset, so the other test retries. Games are independent per seed, so `[..1]` equals the old `exported(1)`.
- **Replay and hashes.** `selfplay` export files are unchanged, because the production budget is still `AI_GATE_BUDGET`. No hidden-information or purity rule is touched, since `jackioh-tools` is not a pure crate.
- **Estimates.** Job times above come from local compile and test timings plus a guessed overhead. After the person's ci.yml edit lands, read the three tools jobs' times on the PR.

## Open questions

**Needs a person: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.** The bot may not edit it. Without these lines the job stays near 5m10, not reliably under 5 minutes. In the `rust-test` matrix, replace the last entry (`group: tools, wasm`) with these three:

```yaml
          - group: tools arena
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '-p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 -- arena:: selfplay_records::'
          - group: tools gate
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '-p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 -- gate::tests::'
          - group: tools, wasm
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '--workspace --exclude jackioh-engine --exclude jackioh-cards --exclude jackioh-server --exclude jackioh-ai --exclude jackioh-luau --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=0 -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions:: --skip arena:: --skip selfplay_records:: --skip gate::tests::'
```

Why these lines:
- **`gate::tests::`, not `gate::`.** The shorter filter also matches 10 `fuzz::tests::fuzz_m4_gate::` tests that `tools fuzz` already runs.
- **Test counts add up.** Old bin tests were 396 (391 passed and 5 ignored): arena 19, `selfplay_records` 2, `gate::tests::` 23 (gate 16 and `duos_gate` 7), and the rest 352. The three groups run exactly those.
- **Opt-levels differ by group.**
  - The catch-all builds the engine at opt-level 1 and the cards at 0, as `engine rules` does. Its workspace compile drops from 178 s to 116 s. Its tests rise from about 40 s to about 56 s.
  - The two AI-game groups keep opt-level 2. At engine 1 and cards 0 their tests took 86 s instead of 51 s.
  - The groups can share the `tools-wasm` cache key, because only workspace crates differ and rust-cache does not store those.

My estimates are roughly 4m for each of the three groups, against 7m30s now. Without the lower opt-levels on the catch-all it would be about 4m47.

In the same ci.yml edit, update the comment above the three tools groups (`in three groups by test name… #1929`) to say: five groups; `tools arena` and `tools gate` run the AI-game modules apart (#3058); `tools, wasm` builds the engine at opt-level 1 and the cards at 0. Also update the header lines in `scripts/ci-scope.sh` that list which groups `rust_tools_wasm` runs (lines 13–14).

**One observation for a person to decide:** `tools duos, selfplay` was not alerted, but `selfplay::` alone takes about 110 s locally, plus `duos_fuzz::`, so it is probably near or over 5 minutes. I did not measure which `selfplay::` tests dominate. The same `play_at` seam could cut them. It is out of this issue's named job, so I left it for you to ask for.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````
